T0526.title: Replay Attack
T0526.definition: An attack that reuses a valid request, event, token, or signature to trigger an operation again.
T0526.description: Replay attacks reuse a still-valid request, signature, token, or event to trigger a business action again. They often affect payment callbacks, webhooks, login tickets, and signed APIs. Effective controls combine nonces, timestamps, signed request scope, one-time tokens, and idempotent processing so old messages cannot be reused.
T0526.usageExample: An attacker captures a payment callback request and replays it, causing the same order to be notified for deduction multiple times; defenders add a one-time nonce and timestamp check in the callback to detect replay attacks.
